Based on the search results, here's what 360Dialog's documentation states about WhatsApp message content access:

## Message Content Access

No message content is shared or sent to WhatsApp at any time and no WhatsApp employee has access to any message content. WhatsApp cannot access any message content exchanged between users and businesses. Once a message is received by the Cloud API, it gets decrypted and forwarded to the business. Messages are only temporarily stored by the Cloud API as required to provide the base API functionality.

## Encryption

When a user sends a message to one of these businesses, the message travels end-to-end encrypted between the user and the Cloud API. As per the Signal protocol, the user and the Cloud API, on behalf of the business, negotiate encryption keys and establish a secure communication channel.

## User Data Handling

Cloud API does not rely on any information about the user (customer/consumer) the business is communicating with other than the phone number used to identify the account. This information is used to deliver the messages via the WhatsApp client code. User phone numbers are used as sources or destinations of individual messages; as such they are deleted when messages are deleted. No other part of Meta has access to this information.

## Can Businesses Read Messages Through WhatsApp Business API?

By default, WhatsApp Business API messages are end-to-end encrypted, so neither Meta nor BSPs can read them - unless the business opts into Meta-hosted services or AI features, which are explicitly disclosed.

Cloud API processes messages on servers in Meta data centers. However, no one in between, not even WhatsApp or Meta, can access the content of your messages, and Meta cannot read the content of your messages at any point during transmission or temporary storage.

## Important Distinction: Transit vs. At Rest

It's important to note that the encryption guarantee is specifically: Meta cannot read message content in transit. However, the moment that message arrives at your webhook endpoint, it's decrypted and your application receives plain text, and from that point on, you're the custodian - if your database isn't encrypted at rest, if your server access controls are lax, if you're logging full message bodies to an unprotected file, that's all on you.

## Encryption Technology

WhatsApp uses the Signal Protocol for end-to-end encryption, which means that only you and the person you are communicating with can read what is sent.
